ko_meaning: 고등학교를 마친 뒤에 한 분야를 깊이 공부하는 학교
ko_meaning_en: A school where you study one field in depth after finishing high school

example.ko: 형은 서울에 있는 대학교에 다녀요.
example.roman: Hyeongeun seoure inneun daehakgyoe danyeoyo.
example.en: My older brother goes to a university in Seoul.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant
-는 turns 있다 into a noun modifier
다니다 + 어요 → 다녀요; N에 다니다 = to attend N

form.q_en: Pick the form of 있다 that can describe 'university'.
form.why: 있다 takes -는 before a noun: 서울에 있는 대학교 = a university in Seoul. 있은 is not used, and -아서/-고 cannot describe a noun.

ko_meaning: 대학교에서 중심으로 공부하는 분야
ko_meaning_en: The field you mainly study at university

example.ko: 제 전공은 한국어인데 아직 말하기가 어려워요.
example.roman: Je jeongongeun hangugeoinde ajik malhagiga eoryeowoyo.
example.en: My major is Korean, but speaking is still hard for me.

tokens.note: -ㄴ데 after a noun + 이다 sets up a contrast

form.q_en: Pick the ending that joins 'is Korean' to the next part with 'but'.
form.ko: 제 전공은 한국어___ 아직 말하기가 어려워요.
form.why: After a noun, -는데 comes as 인데 (이다 + -ㄴ데): 한국어인데 = 'it is Korean, but'. 는데/은데/한데 cannot follow a noun directly.

ko_meaning: 학교에서 한 해를 둘로 나눈 공부 기간
ko_meaning_en: A study period made by dividing the school year into two

example.ko: 다음 학기에는 수업을 더 많이 듣기로 했어요.
example.roman: Daeum hakgieneun sueobeul deo mani deutgiro haesseoyo.
example.en: I decided to take more classes next semester.

tokens.note: 수업을 듣다 = to take a class; -기로 하다 = to decide to

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 듣다 before -기로 했어요.
form.ko: 다음 학기에는 수업을 더 많이 ___ 했어요.
form.why: 듣다 changes ㄷ to ㄹ only before a vowel (들어요). Before -기 the ㄷ stays: 듣기로 하다 = decide to take.

ko_meaning: 학교에서 정해진 공부를 모두 마치다
ko_meaning_en: To finish all the required study at a school

example.ko: 누나는 작년에 대학교를 졸업했어요.
example.roman: Nunaneun jangnyeone daehakgyoreul joreopaesseoyo.
example.en: My older sister graduated from university last year.

tokens.note: N을/를 졸업하다 = to graduate from N

form.q_en: 작년에 means 'last year'. Pick the matching form.
form.why: 작년에 (last year) needs the past tense: 졸업했어요. The other forms are present, future or a request.

ko_meaning: 학생이 되어 학교에 처음 들어가다
ko_meaning_en: To become a student and enter a school for the first time

example.ko: 대학교에 입학했을 때 정말 기뻤어요.
example.roman: Daehakgyoe ipakaesseul ttae jeongmal gippeosseoyo.
example.en: I was really happy when I entered university.

form.q_en: Pick the form that fits before 때 for a past event.
form.why: Before 때 Korean uses -(으)ㄹ: for a past event, 입학했을 때 = when I entered. 한 때/하는 때 are not used, and 해 cannot come before 때.

ko_meaning: 대학교 등에서 교수가 학생들에게 지식을 가르치는 것
ko_meaning_en: A professor teaching knowledge to students at a university or similar place

example.ko: 그 교수님의 강의는 재미있기 때문에 인기가 많아요.
example.roman: Geu gyosunimui ganguineun jaemiitgi ttaemune ingiga manayo.
example.en: That professor's lectures are popular because they are fun.

form.q_en: Pick the word that completes 'because' after -기.
form.ko: 그 교수님의 강의는 재미있기 ___ 인기가 많아요.
form.why: The reason pattern is -기 때문에 (because). It always ends in 에 when it links two clauses.

ko_meaning: 선생님이 학생에게 해 오라고 내 주는 공부나 일
ko_meaning_en: Study or work a teacher gives students to do and hand in

example.ko: 선생님이 이번 과제는 어렵다고 하셨어요.
example.roman: Seonsaengnimi ibeon gwajeneun eoryeopdago hasyeosseoyo.
example.en: The teacher said this assignment is difficult.

form.q_en: Report what the teacher said: 'it is difficult'.
form.why: Adjectives take -다고 in reported speech: 어렵다고. Only action verbs take -(느)ㄴ다고.

ko_meaning: 여러 사람 앞에서 자기 생각이나 조사한 내용을 말하는 것
ko_meaning_en: Talking about your ideas or research in front of many people

example.ko: 발표를 할 때 너무 긴장했어요.
example.roman: Balpyoreul hal ttae neomu ginjanghaesseoyo.
example.en: I was so nervous when I gave the presentation.

tokens.note: 발표를 하다 = to give a presentation

form.q_en: Pick the form that goes before 때 (when).
form.why: The pattern is -(으)ㄹ 때: 할 때 = when (I) do. 한/하는/해 do not go before 때.

ko_meaning: 시험이나 공부의 결과로 받은 점수나 등급
ko_meaning_en: The score or grade you get from exams or study

example.ko: 열심히 공부해서 성적이 많이 올랐어요.
example.roman: Yeolsimhi gongbuhaeseo seongjeogi mani ollasseoyo.
example.en: I studied hard, so my grades went up a lot.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 오르다 (to go up).
form.why: 오르다 is 르 irregular: 르 becomes ㄹㄹ before 아/어, so 오르 + 았어요 → 올랐어요.

ko_meaning: 공부를 잘하거나 돈이 부족한 학생에게 학교 등에서 주는 돈
ko_meaning_en: Money that a school or other group gives to students who study well or need money

example.ko: 대학교 때 장학금을 받은 적이 있어요.
example.roman: Daehakgyo ttae janghakgeumeul badeun jeogi isseoyo.
example.en: I received a scholarship once in college.

form.q_en: Say 'I have received (it) before'.
form.why: Past experience is -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다, so use the past modifier: 받은 적이 있어요.

ko_meaning: 배운 것을 다시 공부하다
ko_meaning_en: To study again what you have learned

example.ko: 오늘 배운 내용을 집에서 복습해 보세요.
example.roman: Oneul baeun naeyongeul jibeseo bokseupae boseyo.
example.en: Try reviewing today's lesson at home.

form.q_en: Pick the form of 복습하다 that goes before 보세요 (try).
form.why: 'Try doing' is -아/어 보다; 하다 verbs become 해: 복습해 보세요.

ko_meaning: 배울 것을 미리 공부하다
ko_meaning_en: To study in advance what you are going to learn

example.ko: 저는 매일 밤 다음 날 배울 내용을 예습해요.
example.roman: Jeoneun maeil bam daeum nal baeul naeyongeul yeseupaeyo.
example.en: Every night I preview what I will learn the next day.

form.q_en: Pick the form of 배우다 for 'the content I will learn'.
form.ko: 저는 매일 밤 다음 날 ___ 내용을 예습해요.
form.why: To describe a noun with a future meaning, use -(으)ㄹ: 배울 내용 = content (I) will learn.

ko_meaning: 글이나 말을 잊지 않게 머릿속에 넣다
ko_meaning_en: To put words or text into your head so you do not forget them

example.ko: 새 단어를 외우는 것은 정말 어려워요.
example.roman: Sae daneoreul oeuneun geoseun jeongmal eoryeowoyo.
example.en: Memorizing new words is really hard.

form.q_en: Turn 'memorize new words' into a noun phrase with 것.
form.why: -는 것 makes a verb into a noun phrase: 외우는 것 = memorizing. 외우기/외워/외우고 cannot come before 것.

ko_meaning: 무엇이 어떤 뜻인지 알다
ko_meaning_en: To know what something means

example.ko: 이 문제는 너무 복잡해서 이해할 수 없어요.
example.roman: I munjeneun neomu bokjapaeseo ihaehal su eopseoyo.
example.en: This problem is so complicated that I can't understand it.

form.q_en: Say 'cannot understand'.
form.ko: 이 문제는 너무 복잡해서 ___ 수 없어요.
form.why: Ability is -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다, so the verb takes -ㄹ: 이해할 수 없어요.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람이 잘 알 수 있게 내용을 쉽게 말해 주다
ko_meaning_en: To tell something clearly so another person can understand it well

example.ko: 선생님이 문법을 쉽게 설명해 주셨어요.
example.roman: Seonsaengnimi munbeobeul swipge seolmyeonghae jusyeosseoyo.
example.en: The teacher explained the grammar in an easy way.

tokens.note: -게 turns an adjective into an adverb

form.q_en: Pick the adverb form 'easily'.
form.why: To describe how someone does something, add -게 to the adjective: 쉽게 = easily. 쉬운 describes a noun.

ko_meaning: 시험에서 필요한 점수를 받아 붙다
ko_meaning_en: To get the score you need on an exam and pass it

example.ko: 시험에 합격하면 부모님이 정말 기뻐하실 거예요.
example.roman: Siheome hapgyeokamyeon bumonimi jeongmal gippeohasil geoyeyo.
example.en: If I pass the exam, my parents will be really happy.

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'if'.
form.why: -(으)면 means 'if': 합격하면 = if I pass. -러 needs a movement verb, -면서 means 'while', and -지만 means 'but'.

ko_meaning: 위에서 아래로 내려오다. 또는 시험이나 면접에 붙지 못하다
ko_meaning_en: To come down from above; or to not pass an exam or interview

example.ko: 준비를 많이 했는데 면접에서 떨어졌어요.
example.roman: Junbireul mani haenneunde myeonjeobeseo tteoreojyeosseoyo.
example.en: I prepared a lot, but I didn't pass the interview.

tokens.note: -는데 shows a result different from what you expected

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'did ..., but'.
form.why: -았/었는데 links a past action to an unexpected result: 했는데 = I did, but. The others mean 'if', 'in order to go' and 'in order to'.

ko_meaning: 잘 모르거나 조심하지 않아서 잘못하는 것
ko_meaning_en: Doing something wrong because you did not know or were not careful

example.ko: 시험에서 작은 실수를 해서 점수가 낮아요.
example.roman: Siheomeseo jageun silsureul haeseo jeomsuga najayo.
example.en: I made a small mistake on the exam, so my score is low.

tokens.note: 실수를 하다 = to make a mistake

form.q_en: Pick the form of 작다 that describes 실수.
form.why: Adjectives describe a noun with -(으)ㄴ: 작은 실수 = a small mistake. -는 is for action verbs.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 이루려고 몸과 마음을 다해 열심히 하다
ko_meaning_en: To work hard with all your body and mind to achieve something

example.ko: 오빠는 좋은 회사에 취직하려고 노력하고 있어요.
example.roman: Oppaneun joeun hoesae chwijikaryeogo noryeokago isseoyo.
example.en: My older brother is working hard to get a job at a good company.

tokens.en: in order to get a job

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'in order to'.
form.why: -(으)려고 means 'in order to' with any verb. -(으)러 is only used with movement verbs like 가다/오다.

ko_meaning: 어려워서 하던 일을 중간에 하지 않기로 하다
ko_meaning_en: To decide to stop something halfway because it is hard

example.ko: 한국어가 어렵지만 절대 포기하지 않을 거예요.
example.roman: Hangugeoga eoryeopjiman jeoldae pogihaji aneul geoyeyo.
example.en: Korean is hard, but I will never give up.

form.q_en: Complete the negative 'will not give up'.
form.why: Long negation is -지 않다, spelled with ㅎ: 포기하지 않을 거예요. 안 is the short form and does not follow -지.

ko_meaning: 돈을 받고 일하는 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place where you work and get paid

example.ko: 직장이 집에서 멀어서 매일 일찍 일어나요.
example.roman: Jikjangi jibeseo meoreoseo maeil iljjik ireonayo.
example.en: My workplace is far from home, so I get up early every day.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 멀다 (to be far).
form.why: The last vowel of 멀 is ㅓ, so it takes -어서: 멀어서 = because it is far.

ko_meaning: 같은 곳에서 함께 일하는 사람
ko_meaning_en: A person who works with you at the same place

example.ko: 회사 동료와 같이 점심을 먹으면서 이야기했어요.
example.roman: Hoesa dongnyowa gachi jeomsimeul meogeumyeonseo iyagihaesseoyo.
example.en: I talked with a coworker while having lunch together.

form.q_en: Pick the correct 'while eating'.
form.why: -(으)면서 means 'while'. After a consonant (먹) add 으: 먹으면서.

ko_meaning: 직장에서 나보다 자리가 높은 사람
ko_meaning_en: A person at work whose position is higher than yours

example.ko: 상사에게 보고서를 보냈는데 아직 연락이 없어요.
example.roman: Sangsaege bogoseoreul bonaenneunde ajik yeollagi eopseoyo.
example.en: I sent the report to my boss, but there's no reply yet.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'to my boss'.
form.ko: 상사___ 보고서를 보냈는데 아직 연락이 없어요.
form.why: With people, 'to' is 에게. 에 is used for places and things, and 에서 means 'at/from' a place.

ko_meaning: 회사에서 한 부서를 책임지는 사람
ko_meaning_en: The person in charge of one department at a company

example.ko: 부장님이 내일 회의는 오후에 한다고 하셨어요.
example.roman: Bujangnimi naeil hoeuineun ohue handago hasyeosseoyo.
example.en: The department head said tomorrow's meeting will be in the afternoon.

form.q_en: Report the statement 'we will hold it in the afternoon'.
form.why: Action verbs take -ㄴ다고 after a vowel and -는다고 after a consonant: 하다 → 한다고.

ko_meaning: 회사를 대표하고 이끄는 가장 높은 사람
ko_meaning_en: The highest person, who represents and leads a company

example.ko: 사장님은 지금 회의실에 계세요.
example.roman: Sajangnimeun jigeum hoeuisire gyeseyo.
example.en: The president is in the meeting room now.

tokens.note: 계시다 = honorific of 있다 (to be somewhere)

form.q_en: Pick the honorific way to say 'is (in the room)'.
form.why: For a respected person being somewhere, 있다 becomes 계시다 → 계세요. 있으세요 is for 'having' something.

ko_meaning: 일할 회사나 직장을 얻다
ko_meaning_en: To get a company or workplace to work at

example.ko: 언니가 은행에 취직해서 가족들이 모두 기뻐했어요.
example.roman: Eonniga eunhaenge chwijikaeseo gajokdeuri modu gippeohaesseoyo.
example.en: My older sister got a job at a bank, so the whole family was happy.

tokens.note: N에 취직하다 = to get a job at N

form.q_en: Pick the ending that gives the reason.
form.why: -아서/어서 gives a reason: 취직해서 = because she got a job. -려고 and -러 show purpose, and -면서 means 'while'.

ko_meaning: 회사 등에서 사람을 직접 만나서 질문하고 평가하는 시험
ko_meaning_en: A test where a company meets a person, asks questions and judges them

example.ko: 내일 면접을 보는데 정장이 없어요.
example.roman: Naeil myeonjeobeul boneunde jeongjangi eopseoyo.
example.en: I have a job interview tomorrow, but I don't have a suit.

tokens.note: 면접을 보다 = to have an interview

form.q_en: Which verb goes with 면접 (to have an interview)?
form.why: The set phrase is 면접을 보다 = to have an interview. 먹다, 타다 and 치다 do not go with 면접.

ko_meaning: 자기의 학력과 경력 등을 적은 서류
ko_meaning_en: A document where you write your education, work history and so on

example.ko: 이력서를 다 쓰면 이메일로 보내 주세요.
example.roman: Iryeokseoreul da sseumyeon imeillo bonae juseyo.
example.en: When you finish writing your resume, please send it by email.

form.q_en: Pick the particle meaning 'by (email)'.
form.ko: 이력서를 다 쓰면 이메일___ 보내 주세요.
form.why: 'By means of' is (으)로. After a vowel or ㄹ use 로: 이메일로.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 하거나 어떤 곳에 들어가고 싶다고 신청하다
ko_meaning_en: To ask to do a job or to join a place

example.ko: 그 회사에 지원해 보기로 했어요.
example.roman: Geu hoesae jiwonhae bogiro haesseoyo.
example.en: I decided to try applying to that company.

tokens.note: N에 지원하다 = to apply to N

form.q_en: Complete 'decided to try applying'.
form.why: 'Decide to' is -기로 하다. Here it joins 지원해 보다 (try applying): 지원해 보기로 했어요.

ko_meaning: 지금까지 해 온 일이나 일한 기간
ko_meaning_en: The work you have done so far, or how long you have done it

example.ko: 이 일은 경력이 있는 사람만 지원할 수 있어요.
example.roman: I ireun gyeongnyeogi inneun saramman jiwonhal su isseoyo.
example.en: Only people with work experience can apply for this job.

form.q_en: Complete 'can apply'.
form.ko: 이 일은 경력이 있는 사람만 지원할 ___ 있어요.
form.why: Ability is -(으)ㄹ 수 있다: 지원할 수 있어요 = can apply. 줄 goes with 알다, and 적 means past experience.

ko_meaning: 일을 하고 한 달마다 받는 돈
ko_meaning_en: Money you get every month for your work

example.ko: 월급을 받으면 부모님께 선물을 사 드릴 거예요.
example.roman: Wolgeubeul badeumyeon bumonimkke seonmureul sa deuril geoyeyo.
example.en: When I get my salary, I'm going to buy my parents a present.

form.q_en: Pick the honorific particle for 'to/for my parents'.
form.ko: 월급을 받으면 부모님___ 선물을 사 드릴 거예요.
form.why: For respected people, 에게 becomes 께: 부모님께. 에 is for places and things.

ko_meaning: 정해진 시간이 지난 뒤 밤까지 회사에서 일하는 것
ko_meaning_en: Working at the company into the night after normal hours

example.ko: 요즘 일이 많아서 매일 야근을 해요.
example.roman: Yojeum iri manaseo maeil yageuneul haeyo.
example.en: I have a lot of work these days, so I work late every night.

form.q_en: Pick the form that gives the reason.
form.why: -아서 gives a reason: 많아서 = because there is a lot. The other forms mean 'while', 'decide to' and '-ly'.

ko_meaning: 회사나 군대 등에서 정해진 기간 동안 쉬는 것
ko_meaning_en: Time off from a company, the army and so on for a set period

example.ko: 이번 여름 휴가 때 가족과 제주도에 가기로 했어요.
example.roman: Ibeon yeoreum hyuga ttae gajokgwa jejudoe gagiro haesseoyo.
example.en: I decided to go to Jeju Island with my family this summer vacation.

tokens.note: N 때 = at the time of N

form.q_en: Say 'decided to go'.
form.ko: 이번 여름 휴가 때 가족과 제주도에 ___ 했어요.
form.why: 'Decide to do' is -기로 하다: 가기로 했어요.

ko_meaning: 일 때문에 다른 곳에 가는 것
ko_meaning_en: Going to another place for work

example.ko: 아빠는 다음 주에 일본으로 출장을 가세요.
example.roman: Appaneun daeum jue ilboneuro chuljangeul gaseyo.
example.en: Dad is going on a business trip to Japan next week.

tokens.note: 출장을 가다 = to go on a business trip

form.q_en: Pick the particle meaning 'to/toward (Japan)'.
form.ko: 아빠는 다음 주에 일본___ 출장을 가세요.
form.why: 'Toward' is (으)로. 일본 ends in a consonant (not ㄹ), so it takes 으로.

ko_meaning: 회사에서 더 높은 자리로 오르다
ko_meaning_en: To move up to a higher position at a company

example.ko: 삼촌이 부장으로 승진했다고 들었어요.
example.roman: Samchoni bujangeuro seungjinhaetdago deureosseoyo.
example.en: I heard my uncle was promoted to department head.

form.q_en: Report a past event: 'that he was promoted'.
form.why: For a past event, add -다고 to the past stem: 승진했 + 다고 → 승진했다고.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 책임지고 하다
ko_meaning_en: To take responsibility for a task and do it

example.ko: 이번 프로젝트는 제가 맡게 됐어요.
example.roman: Ibeon peurojekteuneun jega matge dwaesseoyo.
example.en: I ended up being in charge of this project.

form.q_en: Say 'ended up taking charge'.
form.why: 'End up doing' is -게 되다: 맡게 됐어요.

ko_meaning: 하던 일을 마치다
ko_meaning_en: To complete something you were doing

example.ko: 오늘 안에 이 일을 끝내야 해요.
example.roman: Oneul ane i ireul kkeunnaeya haeyo.
example.en: I have to finish this work today.

form.q_en: 일을 is an object. Pick the verb that can take it.
form.why: 끝내다 takes an object (일을 끝내다). 끝나다 has no object (일이 끝나다). -야 하다 = have to.

ko_meaning: 정해진 때보다 늦게 하려고 뒤로 넘기다
ko_meaning_en: To push something back to do it later than planned

example.ko: 비 때문에 축제를 다음 주로 미뤘어요.
example.roman: Bi ttaemune chukjereul daeum juro mirwosseoyo.
example.en: We postponed the festival to next week because of the rain.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'to (next week)'.
form.ko: 비 때문에 축제를 다음 주___ 미뤘어요.
form.why: The new time you move something to takes (으)로. 주 ends in a vowel, so use 로.

ko_meaning: 다니던 회사나 하던 일을 더 이상 하지 않다
ko_meaning_en: To stop going to a job or doing something you used to do

example.ko: 친구는 회사를 그만두고 카페를 열었어요.
example.roman: Chinguneun hoesareul geumandugo kapereul yeoreosseoyo.
example.en: My friend quit the company and opened a cafe.

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'and then'.
form.why: -고 joins two actions in order: 그만두고 = quit and (then). -면 means 'if', -러 needs a movement verb, and -는 describes a noun.

ko_meaning: 원래 있던 것이 다른 것으로 되다
ko_meaning_en: For something to become something different from what it was

example.ko: 회의 시간이 세 시로 바뀌었다고 해요.
example.roman: Hoeui sigani se siro bakkwieotdago haeyo.
example.en: They say the meeting time has changed to three o'clock.

tokens.note: 셋 becomes 세 before a counter

form.q_en: 시간이 is the subject. Pick the verb that fits 'the time has changed'.
form.why: 바뀌다 (to be changed) has no object, so it goes with 시간이. 바꾸다 (to change something) needs an object with 을/를.

ko_meaning: 병이 나거나 다쳐서 치료를 받는 사람
ko_meaning_en: A person who is ill or hurt and is being treated

example.ko: 의사는 환자의 말을 잘 들어야 해요.
example.roman: Uisaneun hwanjaui mareul jal deureoya haeyo.
example.en: Doctors have to listen carefully to what patients say.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 듣다 before 해요 (have to).
form.why: 듣다 is ㄷ irregular: before a vowel ㄷ becomes ㄹ, so 듣 + 어야 → 들어야.

ko_meaning: 병원에서 의사를 돕고 환자를 돌보는 사람
ko_meaning_en: A person at a hospital who helps doctors and takes care of patients

example.ko: 간호사가 이름을 부르면 들어가세요.
example.roman: Ganhosaga ireumeul bureumyeon deureogaseyo.
example.en: Please go in when the nurse calls your name.

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'when / if'.
form.why: -(으)면 means 'when/if': 부르면 = when (she) calls. -러/-려고 show purpose and -기로 means 'decide to'.

ko_meaning: 의사가 환자의 몸을 살펴보고 병을 알아내는 것
ko_meaning_en: A doctor checking a patient's body to find out what illness they have

example.ko: 의사 선생님께 진찰을 받았는데 감기라고 하셨어요.
example.roman: Uisa seonsaengnimkke jinchareul badanneunde gamgirago hasyeosseoyo.
example.en: I was examined by the doctor, and he said it's a cold.

form.q_en: Report 'it is a cold' (a noun).
form.why: A noun in reported speech takes (이)라고. 감기 ends in a vowel, so use 라고: 감기라고.

ko_meaning: 바늘로 몸 안에 약을 넣는 것
ko_meaning_en: Putting medicine into the body with a needle

example.ko: 아이가 주사를 맞을 때 많이 울었어요.
example.roman: Aiga jusareul majeul ttae mani ureosseoyo.
example.en: The child cried a lot when getting a shot.

tokens.note: 주사를 맞다 = to get a shot

form.q_en: Which verb goes with 주사 (to get a shot)?
form.why: The set phrase is 주사를 맞다 = to get a shot.

ko_meaning: 병을 고치려고 병원에 들어가 지내다
ko_meaning_en: To go into a hospital and stay there to get treated

example.ko: 할머니가 다리를 다쳐서 일주일 동안 입원하셨어요.
example.roman: Halmeoniga darireul dachyeoseo iljuil dongan ibwonhasyeosseoyo.
example.en: Grandma hurt her leg and was in the hospital for a week.

tokens.note: N 동안 = for (a length of time)

form.q_en: Pick the form that gives the reason.
form.why: -아서/어서 gives a reason: 다쳐서 = because she got hurt. 다치 + 어서 → 다쳐서.

ko_meaning: 몸이나 마음에 병이 없고 튼튼한 상태
ko_meaning_en: The state of having a strong body and mind without illness

example.ko: 건강에 좋은 음식을 먹으려고 노력해요.
example.roman: Geongange joeun eumsigeul meogeuryeogo noryeokaeyo.
example.en: I try to eat food that is good for my health.

tokens.note: 건강에 좋다 = good for your health

form.q_en: Pick the particle in 'good for your health'.
form.why: The set phrase is N에 좋다 = good for N: 건강에 좋은 음식.

ko_meaning: 병에 걸렸을 때 몸에 나타나는 여러 가지 변화
ko_meaning_en: The changes that appear in your body when you are sick

example.ko: 감기 증상이 있으면 집에서 쉬세요.
example.roman: Gamgi jeungsangi isseumyeon jibeseo swiseyo.
example.en: If you have cold symptoms, rest at home.

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'if'.
form.why: -(으)면 means 'if'. After a consonant (있) add 으: 있으면.

ko_meaning: 먹은 음식을 몸 안에서 잘게 만들어 몸이 쓸 수 있게 하는 것
ko_meaning_en: Breaking down food inside the body so the body can use it

example.ko: 저녁을 너무 많이 먹어서 소화가 안 돼요.
example.roman: Jeonyeogeul neomu mani meogeoseo sohwaga an dwaeyo.
example.en: I ate too much dinner, so I have indigestion.

tokens.note: 소화가 안 되다 = to have indigestion

form.q_en: Pick the correct spelling of 되다 + -어요.
form.ko: 저녁을 너무 많이 먹어서 소화가 안 ___.
form.why: 되다 + 어요 → 되어요 → 돼요. '되요' is a common spelling mistake, and 해요/대요 have other meanings.

ko_meaning: 어떤 음식이나 물질 때문에 몸이 가렵거나 붓는 등 나쁘게 반응하는 것
ko_meaning_en: The body reacting badly to a food or substance, for example by itching or swelling

example.ko: 저는 땅콩 알레르기가 있어서 조심해야 해요.
example.roman: Jeoneun ttangkong allereugiga isseoseo josimhaeya haeyo.
example.en: I have a peanut allergy, so I have to be careful.

form.q_en: Say 'have to be careful'.
form.why: 'Have to' is -아야/어야 하다; 하다 verbs become 해야: 조심해야 해요.

ko_meaning: 병이 나아서 병원에서 지내는 것을 끝내고 집에 가다
ko_meaning_en: To stop staying at the hospital and go home after getting better

example.ko: 의사 선생님이 다음 주에 퇴원할 수 있다고 하셨어요.
example.roman: Uisa seonsaengnimi daeum jue toewonhal su itdago hasyeosseoyo.
example.en: The doctor said I can leave the hospital next week.

form.q_en: Report 'I can leave'.
form.ko: 의사 선생님이 다음 주에 퇴원할 수 ___ 하셨어요.
form.why: 있다/없다 take -다고 in reported speech: 퇴원할 수 있다고 = that I can leave.

ko_meaning: 몸의 한 부분이 병이나 상처 때문에 부풀어 커지다
ko_meaning_en: For a part of the body to puff up because of illness or injury

example.ko: 어제 라면을 먹고 자서 얼굴이 부었어요.
example.roman: Eoje ramyeoneul meokgo jaseo eolguri bueosseoyo.
example.en: I ate ramen and went to sleep yesterday, so my face is puffy.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 붓다 (to swell).
form.why: 붓다 is ㅅ irregular: ㅅ drops before a vowel, so 붓 + 었어요 → 부었어요.

ko_meaning: 먹은 것을 입 밖으로 다시 내보내다
ko_meaning_en: To bring food you ate back out through your mouth

example.ko: 아이가 열이 나고 토해서 병원에 갔어요.
example.roman: Aiga yeori nago tohaeseo byeongwone gasseoyo.
example.en: The child had a fever and threw up, so we went to the hospital.

tokens.note: 열이 나다 = to have a fever

form.q_en: Pick the form that gives the reason.
form.why: -아서/어서 gives a reason: 토해서 = because (the child) threw up. The others show purpose or a decision.

ko_meaning: 머리가 빙빙 도는 것처럼 느껴지다
ko_meaning_en: To feel as if your head is spinning

example.ko: 머리가 어지러우면 잠깐 앉아서 쉬세요.
example.roman: Meoriga eojireoumyeon jamkkan anjaseo swiseyo.
example.en: If you feel dizzy, sit down and rest for a moment.

form.q_en: Pick the correct 'if' form of 어지럽다.
form.why: 어지럽다 is ㅂ irregular: ㅂ + 으 becomes 우, so 어지럽 + 으면 → 어지러우면.

ko_meaning: 피부를 긁고 싶은 느낌이 있다
ko_meaning_en: To have a feeling that makes you want to scratch your skin

example.ko: 피부가 너무 가려워서 잠을 못 잤어요.
example.roman: Pibuga neomu garyeowoseo jameul mot jasseoyo.
example.en: My skin was so itchy that I couldn't sleep.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 가렵다.
form.why: 가렵다 is ㅂ irregular: ㅂ + 어 becomes 워, so 가렵 + 어서 → 가려워서.

ko_meaning: 의사가 몸을 열거나 잘라서 병을 고치는 일
ko_meaning_en: A doctor treating an illness by opening or cutting the body

example.ko: 할아버지는 다음 주에 무릎 수술을 받으세요.
example.roman: Harabeojineun daeum jue mureup susureul badeuseyo.
example.en: Grandpa is having knee surgery next week.

form.q_en: Pick the correct honorific form of 받다.
form.why: The honorific -(으)세요 takes 으 after a consonant: 받 + 으세요 → 받으세요.

ko_meaning: 살을 빼려고 음식을 적게 먹거나 운동하는 것
ko_meaning_en: Eating less or exercising to lose weight

example.ko: 다이어트를 하는데 자꾸 간식이 먹고 싶어요.
example.roman: Daieoteureul haneunde jakku gansigi meokgo sipeoyo.
example.en: I'm on a diet, but I keep wanting to eat snacks.

tokens.note: 다이어트를 하다 = to be on a diet

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'I'm doing ..., but'.
form.why: -는데 sets up a contrast: 하는데 = I'm doing it, but. The others show purpose or a decision.

ko_meaning: 몸에 살이 붙어 몸무게가 늘다
ko_meaning_en: For your body to get fatter and your weight to go up

example.ko: 운동을 안 하고 많이 먹으면 살찌게 돼요.
example.roman: Undongeul an hago mani meogeumyeon saljjige dwaeyo.
example.en: If you don't exercise and eat a lot, you end up gaining weight.

form.q_en: Say 'you end up gaining weight'.
form.ko: 운동을 안 하고 많이 먹으면 ___ 돼요.
form.why: 'End up doing' is -게 되다: 살찌게 돼요.

ko_meaning: 붙어 있던 것이 떨어져 나오다. 또는 몸의 살이 줄다
ko_meaning_en: For something attached to come out; or for your body to lose weight

example.ko: 한 달 동안 걸어서 출근했는데 살이 빠졌어요.
example.roman: Han dal dongan georeoseo chulgeunhaenneunde sari ppajyeosseoyo.
example.en: I walked to work for a month, and I lost weight.

tokens.note: 하나 becomes 한 before a counter

form.q_en: 살이 is the subject. Pick the verb that fits.
form.ko: 한 달 동안 걸어서 출근했는데 살이 ___.
form.why: 살이 빠지다 has no object (weight comes off). 살을 빼다 needs 을: you lose weight on purpose.

ko_meaning: 오랫동안 되풀이해서 저절로 하게 된 행동
ko_meaning_en: Something you do without thinking because you have repeated it for a long time

example.ko: 자기 전에 핸드폰을 보는 습관을 고치고 싶어요.
example.roman: Jagi jeone haendeuponeul boneun seupgwaneul gochigo sipeoyo.
example.en: I want to fix my habit of looking at my phone before bed.

form.q_en: Pick the form of 보다 that describes 습관 (a repeated action).
form.ko: 자기 전에 핸드폰을 ___ 습관을 고치고 싶어요.
form.why: A habit is something you do regularly, so use the present modifier -는: 보는 습관.

ko_meaning: 담배를 피우지 않음. 또는 담배를 피우지 못하게 함
ko_meaning_en: Not smoking; or not allowing people to smoke

example.ko: 식당 안은 금연이니까 담배는 밖에서 피우세요.
example.roman: Sikdang aneun geumyeoninikka dambaeneun bakkeseo piuseyo.
example.en: It's no smoking inside the restaurant, so please smoke outside.

tokens.note: -(으)니까 can be followed by a request

form.q_en: The sentence ends in a request (-세요). Pick the reason form that fits.
form.why: Before a request or command, use -(으)니까, not -아서/(이)라서: 금연이니까 피우세요.

ko_meaning: 외국에 갈 때 필요한, 나라에서 만들어 주는 신분증
ko_meaning_en: An ID from your country that you need when you go abroad

example.ko: 공항에 가기 전에 여권을 꼭 챙기세요.
example.roman: Gonghange gagi jeone yeogwoneul kkok chaenggiseyo.
example.en: Be sure to take your passport before you go to the airport.

form.q_en: Pick the form that goes before 전에 (before).
form.why: 'Before doing' is -기 전에: 가기 전에 = before going.

ko_meaning: 다른 나라에 들어가거나 머물 수 있게 그 나라가 허락해 주는 문서
ko_meaning_en: A document from a country that lets you enter or stay there

example.ko: 비자를 신청했는데 아직 안 나왔어요.
example.roman: Bijareul sincheonghaenneunde ajik an nawasseoyo.
example.en: I applied for a visa, but it hasn't come out yet.

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'I applied, but'.
form.why: -았/었는데 links a past action to an unexpected result: 신청했는데 = I applied, but.

ko_meaning: 자리나 방, 표 등을 미리 정해 두다
ko_meaning_en: To arrange a seat, room, ticket and so on in advance

example.ko: 식당을 예약하려고 전화했는데 자리가 없었어요.
example.roman: Sikdangeul yeyakaryeogo jeonhwahaenneunde jariga eopseosseoyo.
example.en: I called to book the restaurant, but there were no tables.

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'in order to'.
form.why: -(으)려고 means 'in order to' with any verb. -(으)러 only goes with movement verbs like 가다/오다, not 전화하다.

ko_meaning: 여행할 때 잠을 자고 머무는 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place where you sleep and stay while traveling

example.ko: 숙소가 바다 근처에 있어서 아침마다 산책했어요.
example.roman: Suksoga bada geuncheoe isseoseo achimmada sanchaekaesseoyo.
example.en: Our accommodation was near the sea, so I took a walk every morning.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form. (-아서/어서 never takes the past tense.)
form.why: -아서/어서 does not take the past marker; the last verb shows the tense: 있어서 ... 산책했어요.

ko_meaning: 다른 곳의 경치나 문화 등을 구경하러 다니는 것
ko_meaning_en: Going around to see the scenery, culture and so on of another place

example.ko: 경주로 관광을 간 적이 있어요.
example.roman: Gyeongjuro gwangwangeul gan jeogi isseoyo.
example.en: I have been sightseeing in Gyeongju before.

form.q_en: Say 'I have gone (before)'.
form.why: Past experience is -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다: 가 + ㄴ → 간 적이 있어요.

ko_meaning: 여행이나 이사할 때 가지고 가는 물건
ko_meaning_en: Things you take with you when you travel or move

example.ko: 짐이 너무 무거워서 택시를 탔어요.
example.roman: Jimi neomu mugeowoseo taeksireul tasseoyo.
example.en: My luggage was so heavy that I took a taxi.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 무겁다.
form.why: 무겁다 is ㅂ irregular: 무겁 + 어서 → 무거워서. -아서/어서 never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning: 땅의 모양과 길, 건물 등을 작게 줄여서 그린 그림
ko_meaning_en: A picture that shows land, roads, buildings and so on at a smaller size

example.ko: 길을 모를 때는 지도를 보세요.
example.roman: Gireul moreul ttaeneun jidoreul boseyo.
example.en: When you don't know the way, look at a map.

form.q_en: Pick the form that goes before 때 (when).
form.why: 'When' is -(으)ㄹ 때: 모르 + ㄹ → 모를 때.

ko_meaning: 산이나 바다 등 자연의 아름다운 모습
ko_meaning_en: The beautiful look of nature, such as mountains or the sea

example.ko: 산 위에서 보는 경치가 정말 멋있었어요.
example.roman: San wieseo boneun gyeongchiga jeongmal meosisseosseoyo.
example.en: The view from the top of the mountain was really amazing.

form.q_en: Pick the form of 보다 that describes 경치.
form.why: To describe a noun with a verb, use -는: 보는 경치 = the view (you) see.

ko_meaning: 어떤 곳에 다녀온 것을 기억하려고 사는 물건
ko_meaning_en: Something you buy to remember a place you visited

example.ko: 친구들에게 줄 기념품을 시장에서 샀어요.
example.roman: Chingudeurege jul ginyeompumeul sijangeseo sasseoyo.
example.en: I bought souvenirs at the market to give to my friends.

form.q_en: Pick the form for 'souvenirs (I) will give'.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ describes something for the future: 줄 기념품 = souvenirs I will give. 준 would mean I already gave them.

ko_meaning: 어떤 내용을 알려 주거나 길을 가르쳐 주는 것
ko_meaning_en: Telling someone information or showing them the way

example.ko: 역에 도착하면 안내 방송을 잘 들으세요.
example.roman: Yeoge dochakamyeon annae bangsongeul jal deureuseyo.
example.en: When you arrive at the station, listen carefully to the announcement.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite request form of 듣다.
form.why: 듣다 is ㄷ irregular: before a vowel ㄷ becomes ㄹ, so 듣 + 으세요 → 들으세요.

ko_meaning: 한 나라의 돈을 다른 나라의 돈으로 바꾸다
ko_meaning_en: To change one country's money into another country's money

example.ko: 공항보다 은행에서 환전하는 것이 더 싸요.
example.roman: Gonghangboda eunhaengeseo hwanjeonhaneun geosi deo ssayo.
example.en: Exchanging money at a bank is cheaper than at the airport.

form.q_en: Pick the particle meaning 'than'.
form.ko: 공항___ 은행에서 환전하는 것이 더 싸요.
form.why: 보다 means 'than' in comparisons with 더: A보다 B가 더 싸요 = B is cheaper than A.

ko_meaning: 갔다가 다시 돌아오는 것
ko_meaning_en: Going somewhere and coming back again

example.ko: 서울에서 대전까지 왕복 네 시간쯤 걸려요.
example.roman: Seoureseo daejeonkkaji wangbok ne siganjjeum geollyeoyo.
example.en: A round trip from Seoul to Daejeon takes about four hours.

tokens.note: 넷 becomes 네 before a counter

form.q_en: Pick the correct number for 'four hours'.
form.why: Hours (시간) use native numbers, and 넷 becomes 네 before a counter: 네 시간.

ko_meaning: 가는 것과 오는 것 중에서 한쪽만
ko_meaning_en: Only one direction, either going or coming

example.ko: 부산까지 가는 편도 표를 한 장 주세요.
example.roman: Busankkaji ganeun pyeondo pyoreul han jang juseyo.
example.en: One one-way ticket to Busan, please.

tokens.note: 하나 becomes 한 before a counter

form.q_en: Pick the correct number before the counter 장.
form.ko: 부산까지 가는 편도 표를 ___ 장 주세요.
form.why: Counters like 장 take native numbers, and 하나 becomes 한 before a counter: 한 장.

ko_meaning: 비행기를 탈 수 있는 표
ko_meaning_en: A ticket that lets you get on an airplane

example.ko: 인터넷으로 항공권을 사면 더 싸다고 해요.
example.roman: Inteoneseuro hanggonggwoneul samyeon deo ssadago haeyo.
example.en: They say plane tickets are cheaper if you buy them online.

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'if'.
form.why: -(으)면 means 'if': 사면 = if you buy. -러/-려고 show purpose and -기로 means 'decide to'.

ko_meaning: 한 나라의 안
ko_meaning_en: Inside one country

example.ko: 국내 여행은 비자가 필요 없어서 편해요.
example.roman: Gungnae yeohaengeun bijaga pillyo eopseoseo pyeonhaeyo.
example.en: Domestic travel is convenient because you don't need a visa.

form.q_en: Pick the form that gives the reason.
form.why: -아서/어서 gives a reason: 필요 없어서 = because it is not needed.

en: to date; to make friends with
ko_meaning: 서로 가깝게 지내며 친구나 애인이 되다
ko_meaning_en: To spend time closely with someone and become friends or a couple

example.ko: 한국에서 새 친구를 많이 사귀었어요.
example.roman: Hangugeseo sae chingureul mani sagwieosseoyo.
example.en: I made a lot of new friends in Korea.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 사귀다.
form.why: ㅟ does not merge with 어, so 사귀 + 었어요 → 사귀었어요. '사겼어요' is a common spelling mistake.

ko_meaning: 함께 있던 사람과 떨어지거나, 사귀던 사이가 끝나다
ko_meaning_en: To part from someone, or for a dating relationship to end

example.ko: 남자 친구와 헤어진 후에 많이 울었어요.
example.roman: Namja chinguwa heeojin hue mani ureosseoyo.
example.en: I cried a lot after breaking up with my boyfriend.

form.q_en: Pick the form that goes before 후에 (after).
form.why: 'After doing' is -(으)ㄴ 후에, with the past modifier: 헤어진 후에.

ko_meaning: 두 사람이 서로 사랑하며 사귀는 것
ko_meaning_en: Two people loving each other and going out together

example.ko: 부모님은 오 년 동안 연애하고 결혼하셨어요.
example.roman: Bumonimeun o nyeon dongan yeonaehago gyeolhonhasyeosseoyo.
example.en: My parents dated for five years and then got married.

form.q_en: Pick the correct number for 'five years'.
form.why: 년 (year) uses Sino-Korean numbers: 오 년 = five years.

ko_meaning: 서로 사랑하며 사귀는 사람
ko_meaning_en: A person you love and are dating

example.ko: 애인이 생기면 같이 여행을 가 보고 싶어요.
example.roman: Aeini saenggimyeon gachi yeohaengeul ga bogo sipeoyo.
example.en: If I get a partner, I'd like to try going on a trip together.

form.q_en: Complete 'want to try going'.
form.ko: 애인이 생기면 같이 여행을 가 ___ 싶어요.
form.why: -아/어 보다 (try) + -고 싶다 (want to) → 가 보고 싶어요.

ko_meaning: 처음으로 느끼거나 처음으로 한 사랑
ko_meaning_en: Love that you feel or have for the first time

example.ko: 고등학교 때 첫사랑을 아직 잊지 못했어요.
example.roman: Godeunghakgyo ttae cheotsarangeul ajik itji motaesseoyo.
example.en: I still haven't been able to forget my first love from high school.

form.q_en: Complete 'have not been able to forget'.
form.why: 'Cannot' after -지 is 못하다: 잊지 못했어요. With -지 the 'not' form is 않다, not 안 하다.

ko_meaning: 결혼을 하려고 여는 행사
ko_meaning_en: An event held for two people getting married

example.ko: 이번 주말에 친구 결혼식에 가야 해서 바빠요.
example.roman: Ibeon jumare chingu gyeolhonsige gaya haeseo bappayo.
example.en: I'm busy because I have to go to a friend's wedding this weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the correct present form of 바쁘다.
form.ko: 이번 주말에 친구 결혼식에 가야 해서 ___.
form.why: When ㅡ meets 아/어 it drops. 바 has ㅏ, so add 아요: 바쁘 → 바빠요.

ko_meaning: 결혼식을 올리는 남자
ko_meaning_en: The man who is getting married at a wedding

example.ko: 신랑이 신부를 보면서 환하게 웃었어요.
example.roman: Sillangi sinbureul bomyeonseo hwanhage useosseoyo.
example.en: The groom smiled brightly while looking at the bride.

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'while'.
form.why: -(으)면서 means 'while', for two things one person does at the same time: 보면서 웃었어요.

ko_meaning: 결혼식을 올리는 여자
ko_meaning_en: The woman who is getting married at a wedding

example.ko: 하얀 드레스를 입은 신부가 정말 예뻤어요.
example.roman: Hayan deureseureul ibeun sinbuga jeongmal yeppeosseoyo.
example.en: The bride in the white dress was really beautiful.

tokens.note: past modifier: the state after putting it on

form.q_en: Pick the form of 입다 that describes the bride.
form.why: To describe a noun, the verb needs a modifier ending. 입은 = (who is) wearing, the state after putting it on.

ko_meaning: 아기의 첫 번째 생일에 하는 잔치
ko_meaning_en: A party held on a baby's first birthday

example.ko: 조카의 돌잔치에서 가족 사진을 찍었어요.
example.roman: Jokaui doljanchieseo gajok sajineul jjigeosseoyo.
example.en: We took a family photo at my nephew's first birthday party.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where an action happens.
form.why: The place where you do an action takes 에서: 돌잔치에서 사진을 찍었어요.

ko_meaning: 죽은 사람과 마지막으로 헤어지는 행사
ko_meaning_en: An event for saying a last goodbye to a person who has died

example.ko: 할아버지 장례식에 친척들이 모두 모였어요.
example.roman: Harabeoji jangnyesige chincheokdeuri modu moyeosseoyo.
example.en: All our relatives gathered for Grandpa's funeral.

form.q_en: 친척들이 is the subject. Pick the verb that fits 'gathered'.
form.why: 모이다 (to gather, no object) fits 친척들이. 모으다 → 모았어요 means to collect something and needs an object.

ko_meaning: 두 사물의 가운데. 또는 사람과 사람의 관계
ko_meaning_en: The space between two things; or the relationship between people

example.ko: 저와 언니는 사이가 아주 좋아요.
example.roman: Jeowa eonnineun saiga aju joayo.
example.en: My older sister and I get along really well.

tokens.note: 사이가 좋다 = to get along well

form.q_en: Pick the particle meaning 'and'.
form.why: 와/과 means 'and'. 저 ends in a vowel, so use 와; 과 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning: 둘 이상의 사람이나 물건이 서로 이어져 있는 것
ko_meaning_en: Two or more people or things being connected to each other

example.ko: 두 사람은 무슨 관계예요?
example.roman: Du sarameun museun gwangyeyeyo?
example.en: What is the relationship between the two of them?

tokens.note: 둘 becomes 두 before a noun

form.q_en: Pick the correct spelling of 'is (a) relationship'.
form.why: After a noun ending in a vowel, 이다 becomes -예요: 관계예요. '관계에요' is a common mistake.

ko_meaning: 서로 가깝게 지내며 사이가 좋다
ko_meaning_en: To spend a lot of time together and get along well

example.ko: 민수와 저는 어렸을 때부터 친한 친구예요.
example.roman: Minsuwa jeoneun eoryeosseul ttaebuteo chinhan chinguyeyo.
example.en: Minsu and I have been close friends since we were young.

form.q_en: Pick the form of 친하다 that describes 친구.
form.why: Adjectives describe a noun with -(으)ㄴ: 친한 친구 = a close friend.

ko_meaning: 말이나 힘으로 서로 이기려고 하다
ko_meaning_en: To try to beat each other with words or strength

example.ko: 어제 동생하고 싸워서 지금도 기분이 안 좋아요.
example.roman: Eoje dongsaenghago ssawoseo jigeumdo gibuni an joayo.
example.en: I fought with my younger sibling yesterday, so I'm still in a bad mood.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 싸우다.
form.ko: 어제 동생하고 ___ 지금도 기분이 안 좋아요.
form.why: 우 + 어 → 워, so 싸우 + 어서 → 싸워서. -아서/어서 never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning: 싸움을 멈추고 다시 사이좋게 지내다
ko_meaning_en: To stop fighting and get along well again

example.ko: 싸운 친구와 빨리 화해하고 싶어요.
example.roman: Ssaun chinguwa ppalli hwahaehago sipeoyo.
example.en: I want to make up quickly with the friend I fought with.

form.q_en: Say 'want to make up'.
form.why: 'Want to' is -고 싶다: 화해하고 싶어요.

ko_meaning: 기쁨, 슬픔, 화 등 마음에 생기는 느낌
ko_meaning_en: Feelings that come up in your heart, such as joy, sadness or anger

example.ko: 저는 감정을 말로 표현하는 것이 어려워요.
example.roman: Jeoneun gamjeongeul mallo pyohyeonhaneun geosi eoryeowoyo.
example.en: It's hard for me to express my feelings in words.

form.q_en: Pick the particle meaning 'in/with (words)'.
form.ko: 저는 감정을 말___ 표현하는 것이 어려워요.
form.why: 'By means of' is (으)로. After ㄹ use 로, not 으로: 말로.

ko_meaning: 마음에 생기는 좋거나 나쁜 느낌
ko_meaning_en: A good or bad feeling in your mind

example.ko: 기분이 좋으면 노래를 부르면서 청소해요.
example.roman: Gibuni joeumyeon noraereul bureumyeonseo cheongsohaeyo.
example.en: When I'm in a good mood, I clean while singing.

form.q_en: Pick the correct 'when/if' form of 좋다.
form.why: -(으)면 takes 으 after a consonant: 좋 + 으면 → 좋으면.

en: to be shy; to be embarrassed
ko_meaning: 다른 사람 앞에 서거나 칭찬을 받을 때처럼 얼굴이 빨개지는 느낌이 있다
ko_meaning_en: To have a feeling that makes your face turn red, as when you stand before others or are praised

example.ko: 사람들 앞에서 노래하는 것이 부끄러워요.
example.roman: Saramdeul apeseo noraehaneun geosi bukkeureowoyo.
example.en: Singing in front of people makes me shy.

form.q_en: Pick the correct present form of 부끄럽다.
form.why: 부끄럽다 is ㅂ irregular: ㅂ + 어 becomes 워, so 부끄럽 + 어요 → 부끄러워요.

en: to be ashamed; to be embarrassing
ko_meaning: 실수나 잘못을 해서 다른 사람 보기에 부끄럽다
ko_meaning_en: To feel embarrassed in front of others because of a mistake

example.ko: 길에서 넘어져서 너무 창피했어요.
example.roman: Gireseo neomeojyeoseo neomu changpihaesseoyo.
example.en: I fell down in the street, and it was so embarrassing.

form.q_en: Pick the form that gives the reason.
form.why: -아서/어서 gives a reason: 넘어져서 = because I fell. 넘어지 + 어서 → 넘어져서.

en: to be upset; to feel hurt
ko_meaning: 일이 잘 안 되거나 마음 아픈 일이 있어서 기분이 안 좋다
ko_meaning_en: To feel bad because something went wrong or something hurt you

example.ko: 시험을 잘 못 봐서 너무 속상해요.
example.roman: Siheomeul jal mot bwaseo neomu soksanghaeyo.
example.en: I did badly on the exam, so I'm really upset.

tokens.note: 잘 못 보다 = to do badly (on an exam)
시험을 보다 = to take an exam

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'could not (do well)'.
form.why: 못 + verb means 'could not': 잘 못 봐서 = because I couldn't do well.

ko_meaning: 가까운 사람이 생각만큼 나를 챙겨 주지 않아서 마음이 좋지 않다
ko_meaning_en: To feel sad because someone close did not care for you as much as you expected

example.ko: 친구가 내 생일을 잊어버려서 섭섭했어요.
example.roman: Chinguga nae saengireul ijeobeoryeoseo seopseopaesseoyo.
example.en: I felt let down because my friend forgot my birthday.

form.q_en: Pick the form that gives the reason.
form.why: -아서/어서 gives a reason: 잊어버려서 = because (my friend) forgot.

en: to feel stuffy; to be frustrated
ko_meaning: 숨쉬기 힘들 만큼 막힌 느낌이 있거나, 일이 잘 안 풀려서 마음이 불편하다
ko_meaning_en: To feel closed in, as if it is hard to breathe; or to feel uneasy because things are not going well

example.ko: 방이 좁고 창문이 없어서 답답해요.
example.roman: Bangi jopgo changmuni eopseoseo dapdapaeyo.
example.en: The room is small and has no window, so it feels stuffy.

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'and' to join two facts.
form.why: -고 joins two facts: 좁고 = is small and.

ko_meaning: 무엇을 하는 것이 싫고 힘들게 느껴지다
ko_meaning_en: For doing something to feel annoying and like too much effort

example.ko: 피곤해서 요리하는 것이 귀찮아요.
example.roman: Pigonhaeseo yorihaneun geosi gwichanayo.
example.en: I'm tired, so cooking feels like a hassle.

form.q_en: Pick the correct present form of 귀찮다.
form.why: 귀찮다 keeps its ㄶ and has ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 귀찮아요 (pronounced 귀차나요).

ko_meaning: 기대가 되어 마음이 들뜨고 두근거리다
ko_meaning_en: For your heart to beat fast because you are looking forward to something

example.ko: 내일 첫 데이트가 있어서 너무 설레요.
example.roman: Naeil cheot deiteuga isseoseo neomu seolleyo.
example.en: I have my first date tomorrow, so I'm so excited.

form.q_en: Pick the correct present form. (The base form is 설레다.)
form.why: The base form is 설레다, so the polite form is 설레요. '설레여요' comes from the wrong form '설레이다'.

ko_meaning: 보고 싶거나 다시 만나고 싶은 마음이 크다
ko_meaning_en: To strongly want to see someone or something again

example.ko: 외국에 살면서 엄마가 해 준 음식이 그리워요.
example.roman: Oeguge salmyeonseo eommaga hae jun eumsigi geuriwoyo.
example.en: Living abroad, I miss the food my mom made for me.

form.q_en: Pick the correct 'while living' form of 살다.
form.ko: 외국에 ___ 엄마가 해 준 음식이 그리워요.
form.why: Verbs ending in ㄹ do not add 으: 살 + 면서 → 살면서.
